                                        DIRECT TESTIMONY OF

                                         MICHAEL MARCHAND

                                             ON BEHALF OF

                                             WALMART INC.



                                         SEPTEMBER 18, 2026
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 2 OF 11

                                                                                    Walmart Inc.
                                                           Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand
                                                                     Cause No. PUD 2026-000046

        1      Q.     PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, BUSINESS ADDRESS, AND
        2             OCCUPATION.

        3      A.     My name is Michael Marchand. My business address is 814 Respect

        4             Drive, Bentonville, AR, 72716.         I am employed by Walmart Inc.

        5             (“Walmart”) as Director, State Regulatory.

        6      Q.     ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU TESTIFYING IN THIS DOCKET?

        7      A.     I am testifying on behalf of Walmart.

        8      Q.     PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE.

        9      A.     I have twenty-eight years of business experience, the last fifteen of which I

      10              held various positions with the Arkansas Public Service Commission’s

      11              General Staff (“Staff”). For thirteen years prior to joining Staff, I worked in

      12              the investment banking industry, predominantly as an institutional trader

      13              and equity analyst. I was registered with the Financial Industry Regulatory

      14              Authority and held Series 7, 55, and 63 securities licenses. I joined the Staff

      15              in February 2011 as a Financial Analyst in the Financial Analysis section.

      16              In July 2014, I was promoted to the position of Senior Analyst in the

      17              Research and Policy Section. While in that position, I was appointed to the

      18              National Association of Regulatory and Utility Commissioners (“NARUC”)

      19              Subcommittee on Electricity and elected as a Segment 9 voting member of

      20              the North American Electric Reliability Corporation. I also participated in

      21              working groups and attended meetings of the two Regional Transmission

      22              Organizations (“RTOs”) located in Arkansas. I have received extensive


                                                       1
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 3 OF 11

                                                                                    Walmart Inc.
                                                           Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand

        1             training and professional development, including completion of both the

        2             Annual Regulatory Studies Program in 2011 and the Advanced Regulatory

        3             Studies Program in 2017, both offered through the Institute of Public Utilities

        4             at Michigan State University. I have been an active member of the Society

        5             of Utility Regulatory Financial Analysts for fifteen years and have earned

        6             the Certified Rate of Return Analyst Certification, which is awarded based

        7             upon professional experience and successfully passing a written exam. I

        8             hold a Master of Business Administration degree with a Finance

        9             Concentration from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock and a Bachelor

      10              of Science degree with a major in Finance from Louisiana Tech University.

      11              A copy of my curriculum vitae is attached hereto as Exhibit MM-1.

      12       Q.    HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY BEFORE THE

      13             MARYLAND PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION ("COMMISSION")?

      14       A.    No, this is my first time filing testimony before the Commission.

      15       Q.    HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY BEFORE OTHER

      16             STATE REGULATORY COMMISSIONS?

      17       A.     Yes. In my fifteen years with the Arkansas Public Service Commission, I

      18              filed testimony in numerous dockets on subjects including cost of capital,

      19              revenue requirement, tariff issues, and storm securitization. I have also filed

      20              testimony with the Louisiana Public Service Commission, the Virginia State

      21              Corporation Commission, and the Wisconsin Public Service Commission.



                                                       2
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 4 OF 11

                                                                                          Walmart Inc.
                                                                 Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand
                                                                           Cause No. PUD 2026-000046

        1               A list of dockets in which I have testified is attached as Exhibit MM-1.

        2       Q.      PLEASE        BRIEFLY       DESCRIBE         WALMART’S            OPERATIONS   IN

        3               OKLAHOMA.


        4       A.      As shown on Walmart’s website1, Walmart operates 134 retail units, four

        5               supply chain facilities, and employs over 35,000 associates in Oklahoma.

        6               In fiscal year ending 2025, Walmart purchased $604.9 million worth of

        7               goods and services from over 300 Oklahoma based suppliers, supporting

        8               over 19,000 supplier jobs.

        9       Q.      WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

      10        A.      The purpose of my testimony is to present Walmart’s response to the

      11                proposed Extra Large Load and Light Tariff (“XLPL”) proposed by

      12                Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company (“OG&E” or “Company”). Walmart

      13                generally supports the proposed provisions of XLPL but has concern that

      14                the proposed definition of Large Load Customer is not consistent with the

      15                definition of Large Load Customer set forth in House Bill 2992 of 2026 (“HB

      16                2992”).

      17        Q.      DOES WALMART SUPPORT THE THRESHOLD SET BY THE XLPL OF

      18                75 MEGAWATTS (“MW”) OF EXPECTED PEAK DEMAND IN THE




            1 https://corporate.walmart.com/about/location-facts/united-states/oklahoma




                                                             3
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 5 OF 11

                                                                                     Walmart Inc.
                                                            Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand
                                                                      Cause No. PUD 2026-000046

        1             DEFINITION OF LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER PROPOSED IN XLPL?

        2      A.     Yes. While I am not an attorney, setting the applicability threshold at 75

        3             MW floor is consistent with my understanding of the intent of HB 2992.

        4             Setting the threshold too low creates a significant risk of inadvertently

        5             capturing standard, stable commercial and industrial customers in the XLPL

        6             despite the stated goal of the HB 2992, also known as the Data Center

        7             Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026. Section 3 of the new law,

        8             states:

       9                         Any applicable governing body responsible for
      10                         reviewing electric supplier rates shall ensure that
      11                         residential, commercial, and industrial customers are
      12                         protected from paying unjust rates resulting directly
      13                         from electric service to large load customers.


      14              Modern omnichannel retail providers like Walmart are increasingly utilizing

      15              automated distribution or fulfillment operations, including refrigerated food

      16              distribution, that integrate electric trailer plugs and electric vehicle charging.

      17              The combined demand of these highly integrated, electrification-focused

      18              commercial facilities can approach or exceed 50 MW over a planning

      19              horizon. In Oklahoma, the legislature wisely established a higher threshold

      20              of 75 MW, which provides a necessary regulatory buffer that prevents

      21              standard retail and commercial distribution centers from being swept into a

      22              tariff focused on more speculative loads, while still ensuring that system-

      23              impacting data centers and cryptocurrency operations are fully captured.


                                                        4
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 6 OF 11

                                                                                   Walmart Inc.
                                                          Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand
                                                                    Cause No. PUD 2026-000046

        1             Long-term this policy might stimulate innovation and promote electrification

        2             efforts of larger commercial and industrial customers.

        3      Q.     WHAT CONCERN DOES WALMART HAVE WITH THE PROPOSED

        4             DEFINITION OF LARGE LOAD CUSTOMER IN THE XLPL?

        5      A.     Walmart’s primary concern is that neither the definition of Large Load

        6             Customer proposed in the XLPL nor the definition of Customer in the Terms

        7             and Conditions of Service For Extra Large Load Customers (“T&CXLLC”)

        8             expressly excludes residential, commercial, agricultural, or industrial

        9             ratepayers from applicability of the new tariff, as prescribed in the Data

      10              Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026. While I am not an

      11              attorney, plain reading of HB 2992 shows the intent of the legislature was

      12              for the law to address specific customers as the term Large Load Customer

      13              is defined as:

      14                        4. “Large load customer” means new data centers, new
      15                        cryptocurrency mining operations and new facilities
      16                        whose primary function is artificial-intelligence
      17                        computing facilities that contract with an electric
      18                        supplier to add seventy-five (75) megawatts or greater
      19                        electric load per facility or in aggregate behind a single
      20                        point of interconnection to an electric supplier’s load
      21                        after July 1, 2026. It does not include residential,
      22                        commercial, agricultural, or industrial ratepayers, or
      23                        those entities that build generation for behind-the-




                                                      5
 CASE PUD 2026-000046 ENTRY NO. 33 FILED IN OCC COURT CLERK'S OFFICE ON 09/18/2026 - PAGE 7 OF 11

                                                                                       Walmart Inc.
                                                              Direct Testimony of Michael Marchand
                                                                        Cause No. PUD 2026-000046

        1                          meter projects (emphasis added);2
        2

        3                The Commission should require the Company to amend the proposed

        4                definitions of both the term Large Load Customer in the XLPL and the term

        5                Customer in the T&CXLLC to conform to the statute by adding language

        6                that specifically excludes residential, commercial, agricultural, and industrial

        7                ratepayers, or entities that build generation for behind-the-meter projects.

        8         Q.     DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR TESTIMONY?

        9         A.     Yes.
